clue.text: Obscure? Easily picked up within borders of country

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the borders of a word are its outermost letters, so only the ends of country are used

parts.note: a sound that is easily picked up by the ear is loud

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about something faint that you can hear clearly enough within a nation's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUD sits within C and Y, the borders of 'country'; no word signals the insertion beyond 'within', which links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy liquid or thinking is murky and unclear, just as obscure things are hard to make out.

clue.text: Like an easy job? Copper's retiring

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's stands for 'is', joining the two halves
a retiring person is shy and keeps out of the limelight

explanation.surface: A policeman (copper) is retiring, and the clue wonders whether his job was a soft one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is a comfortable, undemanding post, informal British usage.

clue.text: Get better of several deliveries with an edge, bagging 50

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

indicators.note: bagging means pocketing or enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hem is the finished edge of a piece of cloth
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a bowler's overs find the edge of the bat while the batter reaches a half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six balls bowled in cricket. 'bagging' puts L inside HEM to make HELM.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an opponent is to overpower or defeat them completely.

clue.text: Stop cleaner hiding man

indicators.note: the cleaner's name is shown with the man concealed, so his letters drop out of view

parts.note: detergent is a cleaning agent
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady stops at a house where a man is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' takes GENT out of DETERGENT, leaving DETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off or prevent them acting, so it means stop as a verb.

clue.text: Predict supporting online performers?

parts.note: if you are for something you support it
E- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail
the cast is the group of performers in a show

explanation.surface: A puzzle about guessing what support an internet act will get.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to say in advance what will happen, as weather presenters do.

clue.text: Top removed from prison cells? That's an error

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for prison cells is taken away

parts.note: coop is slang for a prison or confined cell

explanation.surface: Taking the roof off prison cells sounds like a regrettable blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: COOPS loses its top letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation people make on noticing a slip or mistake.

clue.text: Energy and force about Frenchmen in online business

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for force goes round the Frenchmen

parts.note: to coerce is to force someone
MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: A business plan for selling online that relies on drive, compulsion and some French staff.
explanation.walkthrough: MM, short for Messieurs, is the French plural of Monsieur, hence 'Frenchmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: E-commerce is buying and selling conducted over the internet.

clue.text: Father disembarks from tender, moving nimbly

indicators.note: getting off a boat means the father's letters leave the word for tender

parts.note: something tender and easily hurt is fragile
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest climbs out of a small boat (a tender) with surprising ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a boat but means delicate: FRAGILE loses FR.
explanation.definitionFit: An agile person is light and quick on their feet, able to move nimbly.

clue.text: Old work in attempt to support the belief system

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting part sits below the word it holds up
in places the work inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as in a coconut shy
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An old book written to back up a creed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to support' places the lower part beneath 'the'; a shy is a try, as at a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy, a system of belief about the divine.

clue.text: A lunar location, mostly pleasant, set up in approach to filming

indicators.note: in a down answer set up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mare is a dark plain on the Moon, such as the Sea of Tranquillity

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A film crew picks an agreeable spot on the Moon for their shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NICE to NIC; A MARE NIC is then read upwards ('set up').
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama is a widescreen film process using three projectors, a technique for making and showing movies.

clue.text: Street includes area that's sheltered — from this, perhaps

definitions.text: Street includes area that's sheltered — from this, perhaps

indicators.note: includes means the street abbreviation holds the area inside it

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A street has a covered spot where people shelter from bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the lee is where you would shelter from icy precipitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is wintry rain mixed with snow, the kind of weather people take cover from.

clue.text: Work with what's given? I'm in favour of US tool

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped
pro means in favour of
vise is the American spelling of vice, the clamping tool

explanation.surface: Someone declares support for an American workshop tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A vice is a bench clamp; Americans spell it VISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make do with whatever is to hand, without preparation.

clue.text: Certainly will accept first couple of tradescantia amongst little leafy plants

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the word for certainly holds the rest

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: amongst places the letters among those of the word for little

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: the first two letters of the plant's name are taken

explanation.surface: A gardener happily adds some tradescantia to a bed of small foliage plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'amongst' works inside 'will accept'. Wee is Scottish for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are evergreen conifers with dense dark foliage, so they are leafy plants.

clue.text: Area for blokes touring one French city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for blokes surrounds the one

parts.note: men's means belonging to or for men
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A district set aside for men who are on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts I inside MENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in Picardy in northern France.

clue.text: Hint: Minister should dismiss scoundrel

indicators.note: the minister's word sends away the scoundrel's letters

parts.note: a curate is an assistant minister in the Church
a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Advice that a government minister ought to sack a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests government but means clergyman: CURATE loses RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or signal, a hint about what to do next.

clue.text: Cool guy has to accept workplace injury, getting emotional relief

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a cool man

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the clue's has holds the injury

parts.note: RSI is repetitive strain injury, typical of desk work

explanation.surface: A laid-back man hurt at work finds the experience a release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is fodder here, not a link word; 'to accept' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the release of pent-up feelings, a purging of the emotions.

clue.text: Here's what, at sea, starts to identify precipitation?

definitions.text: Here's what, at sea, starts to identify precipitation?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
the opening letters of the next two words are used

explanation.surface: Pointing out the vessel that spots rain coming on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles HERESWHAT into WEATHERSH; IP are the starts of 'identify precipitation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather ship is a vessel stationed in the ocean to take meteorological readings, rainfall included.

clue.text: Means to dismiss a lecturer — using what?

indicators.note: dismiss sends away the a and the lecturer from the word for means

parts.note: the wherewithal is the money or means needed

explanation.surface: A college asks how it could get rid of a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: WHEREWITHAL loses A and L at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherewith is an old word asking with which thing, by what instrument.

clue.text: Employ the writer to interrupt beloved residents

indicators.note: interrupt means break into, so these letters go inside the word for beloved

parts.note: hon is short for honey, a term of endearment
to employ something is to use it
the writer refers to the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: A householder hires the author to interrupt a sweetheart's tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' puts USEME inside HON. Housemen are junior hospital doctors in Britain, called residents in America.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage a resident is a junior hospital doctor, which the British call a houseman.

clue.text: Get used to a beaut hit, knocked for six

indicators.note: knocked for six means devastated or thrown about, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A cricketer's lovely shot is smashed for six runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six is a hit clearing the boundary; 'knocked for six' (badly shaken) is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To habituate is to make or become accustomed to something through repetition.

clue.text: Paint, true, when splashed around, gives measure of warmth

parts.note: tempera is a paint made with egg yolk

indicators.note: splashed around suggests letters flung about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist splashes paint about and it shows how warm the studio is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' is a specific kind here: tempera, the egg-based medium of early Renaissance panels.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperature is the degree of heat or cold, how hot something is.

clue.text: Working to offload second purchase

indicators.note: offload means get rid of, so the second goes from the word for working

parts.note: busy means occupied, working

explanation.surface: A busy person wants to sell off a second purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSY loses S.
explanation.definitionFit: A buy is something bought, a purchase, as in a good buy.

clue.text: A Republican will cover range of points in response

indicators.note: cover means go around, so the a and the Republican wrap the points

parts.note: the compass points north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: A Republican candidate promises to address several issues in a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will cover' puts NSWE between A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply or response to a question.

clue.text: Lad has invested almost everything in hairdressing shop

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, so the boy's word holds the rest

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy

indicators.note: almost cuts the last letter from the word

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A young man has put nearly all his money into a hairdresser's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' reads like money put into a business, but it signals one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business offering hairdressing or beauty services.

clue.text: What's in wet areas, affected by storms?

definitions.text: What's in wet areas, affected by storms?

indicators.note: storms toss things about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Asking what fills flooded places after storms.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the oceans are wet areas, churned up by storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Seawater is the salt water filling the oceans, the wet parts of the globe.

clue.text: Succeed despite your initially being nervous

parts.note: to win is to succeed

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Encouragement to triumph even though you are anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Windy is informal British for scared or jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is British slang for frightened or jumpy, a sense of nervous.

clue.text: Bearing up, consuming American orange juice and wine

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the other letters go inside
in a down answer up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is someone's bearing or manner
OJ is American shorthand for orange juice

explanation.surface: Someone stands tall while drinking juice and wine at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing up' looks like a phrase for coping, but splits: 'Bearing' is the word, 'up' the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of Spain.

clue.text: Practise heading off downpour

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the word for practise goes

parts.note: to train is to practise

explanation.surface: Sports training called off because of a cloudburst.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIN loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is heavy rain, falling water from clouds.

clue.text: Wise to restrain mischievous child — I'm offering personal view

indicators.note: restrain means hold in, so the wise word holds the rest

parts.note: sage means wise
an elf is a small mischievous person, often a child
the apostrophe is dropped

explanation.surface: A wise parent holds back a naughty child and gives an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: An elf as a mischievous child is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Your self-image is how you see yourself, a view of your own person.

clue.text: Marsh, perhaps, never accommodating a lot of steps?

indicators.note: accommodating means holding inside, so the word for never takes the rest in

parts.note: no means not ever, never

indicators.note: a lot of means most, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking, a pattern of steps

explanation.surface: A wetland that never seems to need many steps to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marsh' is the crime novelist Ngaio Marsh, not a bog; 'a lot of' trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand crime writer Dame Ngaio Marsh is the example the question mark signals.

clue.text: Second article in French about climb in good weather

indicators.note: about means around, so the article surrounds the climb

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article
to shin up is to climb

explanation.surface: Another French article about climbing in fine weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' gives S as the time unit, not the ordinal; the final 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunshine is bright sunny weather, the fine conditions everyone hopes for.

clue.text: Limits to healthy GM-free India given by health icon

indicators.note: the limits of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A slogan for a healthy India free of genetically modified crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'healthy', 'GM-free' and 'India' give HY, GE, IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygeia was the Greek goddess of health, daughter of Asclepius, an emblem of wellbeing.
